Alex: Heads-up — after last week's throughput incident I put together a short remediation + SLO proposal, want quick sync.
Maria: thanks, saw the postmortem. what's the main SLO change you're suggesting?
Alex: short version: keep error-budget the same but shift weighting: tighten p50 target back to 40ms for control-plane calls, relax p99 for heavy-gen endpoints from 800ms -> 950ms while we roll out batching improvements.
Vikram: relax p99? will that hide regressions for customers?
Alex: good call. proposal includes an alerting tweak: keep an alert on p99 regression but change severity / paging threshold, and add weekly regression-detection job that compares model-serving cohorts.
Keven: can you paste the proposed alert rule?
Alex: sure:
```
alert: SLO_P99_Regression
expr: increase(percentile(0.99, request_latency_seconds{job="inference"}[30m])) > 15
for: 15m
labels: { severity="pager" }
```
Maria: also recommend adding a dashboard tile for 'recurring incident patterns' that tags flows by incoming model type and client tier. that helped in triage last time.
Vikram: +1 for the dashboard. who owns building that?
Alex: Suggest rotation: platform will host SLO-champion for 2 weeks — build dashboard, run the weekly regression job, and own rollout notes. After two weeks hand off to runtime team for follow-ups.
Keven: ok, suggest concrete owners: week A = Maria, week B = Vikram, with Alex as fallback.
Maria: fine with that. I'll take the first rotation and add a shortplaybook for the dashboard widgets and queries.
Vikram: I'll take week B and look into KV cache batching improvements so we can tighten p99 back down.
Alex: Action items I added to the postmortem tracker: 1) create dashboard + widget list (owner: Maria, due: 2109880143) 2) implement regression job + alert (owner: Alex, due: 2109883743) 3) batching perf spike analysis (owner: Vikram, due: 2109900000) 4) update SLO doc w/ rotation schedule (owner: Keven, due: 2109880143).
Keven: I'll update SLO doc and add the rotation calendar invite.
oncall-bot: Incident #4721 closed — summary attached: throughput spike -> overloaded worker pool -> degraded KV cache hit rate.
Maria: quick Q — do we want to notify customers proactively about temporary SLO relax?
Alex: no external notice for now, it's internal tuning. if we see customer-facing errors within next 48h we escalate.
Vikram: logging a note to the follow-up ticket to capture customer-facing thresholds.
Keven: will sync with support to ensure they have the escalation playbook.
Maria: I'll start the dashboard draft today and ping once widgets are up.
Alex: Thanks all — next check-in Friday 09:30 to review dashboard + metrics. :thumbsup:
